title: Generate All Subsequences of a String
statement:
Given a string `S` of lowercase English letters, generate all of its subsequences.

A **subsequence** is obtained by deleting zero or more characters from `S` without changing the order of the remaining ones. Different choices of deleted positions may produce the same text (in `aab`, deleting either `a` gives `ab`), so list each distinct subsequence only once.

The empty subsequence is not listed. Print the subsequences in **lexicographic (dictionary) order**, where a string comes before every longer string that it is a prefix of (`a` before `ab`).

The expected approach is the `O(2^n)` brute-force recursion: at each position either take the character or skip it. The strings are short enough for this.
inputFormat: A single line containing the string `S`.
outputFormat: Print every distinct non-empty subsequence of `S`, one per line, in lexicographic order.
constraints: S consists of lowercase English letters

examples.output:
a
ab
abc
ac
b
bc
c
examples.explanation: Three distinct letters give 2^3 - 1 = 7 non-empty subsequences. In dictionary order `a` < `ab` < `abc` < `ac` < `b` < `bc` < `c`.
Taking the first `a` or the second `a` alone both yield `a`, and either one with `b` yields `ab`, so duplicates are printed once. Only 5 distinct subsequences remain.
